newsitem.title: UK: Copper sags to lower close, other LME metals mixed.
newsitem.headline: Copper sags to lower close, other LME metals mixed.

text.p: Copper prices dropped during late Tuesday LME trading, with the market's failure at overhead resistance sending it towards the lower end of the current range, traders said.
An unsurprising 3,050-tonne stock fall and a narrowing cash/threes backwardation contributed to a soggy tone, and there could be further falls in the short-term.
"That close does not bode well for copper...the thing is there is no fundamental news at the moment, just gossip," Angus MacMillan, analyst at LME trader Billiton Metals Ltd said.
Three months prices closed at $2,345 a tonne, down $13 from Monday's kerb, but in subsequent late trade shed another $10.

The tin market was well supported, initially by a 280-tonne stock fall, but also by narrowing spreads. Cash/threes, around $40 contango on Monday, contracted to around $10 at one point before being indicated at $7/17.
May/three months moved into a backwardation of some $13, compared with a small $1 contango overnight.
Although forward prices pushed higher, the market encountered resistance at the psychological $6,000 level. Last trade was at $5,970, up $90.
Aluminium similarly trended higher, supported by a reasonable 2,975-tonne stock fall, some short-covering, and steady physical premiums. The market closed at $1,675, up $18.
Nickel prices fluctuated around the $8,000 level, but generally lacked definite direction after an inconclusive 18-tonne increase in stocks.
However, the market was largely trading around the higher end of the day's band, ending at $8,030, still down $35 from the previous kerb.
"It will hold up - just - until the Norilsk situation becomes clearer," MacMillan said.
The zinc market was helped by a 1,025-tonne inventory fall, although business was not particularly active. Prices were maintained on dips under $1,250, closing at $1,251, up $2.
Lead conditions were lacklustre, and the market consequently held in tight range. Final trade was at $670, down $5.
Alloy was quiet, closing at $1,553/55 a tonne, up from Tuesday.
